scope: Qualify cartridge-bus DMA during IRQ discarded fetches; tests and diagnostic adapters only
hardware: Linux x86_64 cloud host; JDK 21.0.8; Maven 3.9.11; C++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror
assets: Generated ADD streams and a NOP BIOS handler, no user ROM/BIOS

matrix.offsets: 0x20, 128-KiB physical page minus two instructions, minus one instruction, and page start
matrix.prefetch_setups: Off, enabled with sequential stream, enabled plus 24 internal idle cycles
matrix.dma: Channel 3, one word from Game Pak 0x08001000 to IWRAM 0x03001000
matrix.input_contract: Logical pipeline is primed before the observed interval; assert IRQ input and normalized raw DMA readiness. This does not qualify peripheral activation, IRQ propagation or handler return-stream invalidation.
matrix.outputs: Elapsed guest cycles, retired handler PC/CPSR/LR/r0 and completed data transfer; Java regressions additionally require two retirements and no unfinished fetch/refill.

validation.native_scope: Jupiter and the standalone adapter execute isolated retained ECJ/CLDC core classes on the host JVM, without host-core fallback. Portable/native source inputs are unchanged; no new SDK build or phone performance claim is required.

reproduction: Build existing tools/nba-reference CMake target nba-cpu-irq-prefetch-probe and run --cartridge-dma. Compile tools/CpuIrqPrefetchProbe.java and run with the same option against host or isolated CLDC classes. Default no-option output remains compatible.
next: Qualify subsequent fetch streams, self-modifying/pipeline latching and IRQ mask/propagation behavior independently; retain the separate natural-LCD timing gate.
release_policy: No tag or release ZIP; v0.9.0 remains immutable.
